ai.description: *Hemiphyllodactylus kolliensis* is a slender gecko reaching 35–40 mm SVL. It is brownish-grey with a dark lateral stripe and a pale tail tip. Key features include a notched snout and 4–5 subdigital lamellae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemiphyllodactylus kolliensis* is best distinguished by its unique combination of a high number of subdigital lamellae and a distinctively short, unsegmented tail base.
ai.habitat: *Hemiphyllodactylus kolliensis* is endemic to the Kolli Hills in India, inhabiting moist deciduous forests and rocky outcrops at elevations between 1,000 and 1,300 meters.
ai.behavior: *Hemiphyllodactylus kolliensis* is a strictly nocturnal gecko that spends its nights foraging for small invertebrates among rock crevices and tree bark.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemiphyllodactylus kolliensis* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two hard-shelled, spherical eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemiphyllodactylus kolliensis* is endemic to the Kolli Hills in the Eastern Ghats of Tamil Nadu, India, occurring at elevations between 1,000 and 1,300 meters.
